2610.12596.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
2610.12596.paper_summary: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck. We introduce SpireBench, in which models play the complete commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire (StS), where early decisions decide long-term success. Across 20 large language models (LLMs) at the game's highest difficulty, frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match the average human player but remain far behind experts. This gap widens as the run lengthens: the strongest models win the first act as often as experts, then fall behind. What separates strong models from weak is how well they play each fight; all of them misjudge risk over a run, preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger. A comprehensive, self-consistent renaming of every game term shows that part of their performance rests on prior knowledge of the game, and models do not improve from the memories they write across runs, which are often wrong and overly cautious. Our harness is the first to give a model the complete original game, and we compare it with existing harnesses. Overall, SpireBench offers an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark with tools to locate where and why agents fail.
2610.12596.paper_summary_zh: 代理大型語言模型現在可以處理複雜的任務，但對於長期的戰略推理仍然研究不足：大多數代理基準都是短期和情節性的，對於長期任務的表現難以拆解為儲存的知識、推理和運氣。我們介紹了SpireBench，在這裡模型玩完整的商業卡牌建造遊戲《Slay the Spire》(StS)，早期的決策決定了長期的成功。在遊戲的最高難度下，20個大型語言模型(LLMs)中，前沿模型超越了啟發式基準，並與平均人類玩家相匹配，但仍然遠遠落後於專家。隨著遊戲進程的延長，這一差距擴大：最強的模型在第一幕的勝率與專家相當，但隨後落後。強模型與弱模型之間的區別在於它們在每場戰鬥中的表現；所有模型在整個過程中都錯誤評估風險，保持健康而不是花費它來變得更強。對每個遊戲術語進行全面、自洽的重新命名顯示，它們的部分表現依賴於對遊戲的先前知識，而模型並未從它們在過程中寫下的記憶中改進，這些記憶往往是錯誤的和過於謹慎的。我們的系統是第一個給模型提供完整原始遊戲的系統，我們將其與現有的系統進行比較。總體而言，SpireBench提供了一個未飽和的長期基準，並提供工具來定位代理失敗的原因和位置。
